A detached raised black speck follows that terminal before the closing parenthesis; its separation does not securely distinguish a prime from a broken terminal stroke.

After the tall opening-parenthesis curve, the argument itself has one shallow trough and ends rising at the right. Same-page w has two internal troughs, while clear u ends with a downward terminal; neither distinguishing extra stroke occurs here.

A tall first 1 precedes overlapping closed loops; the dominant right stroke descends well below them and turns far left, supporting a final 9. The extra upper/lower loop remnants may be an overwritten 8, but their separate extent is not secure, so that layer remains uncertain rather than being asserted as a complete earlier 18.

There is a separate dark dot above-left of the index body, favoring a dotted letter. The lower body is doubled or overtraced, with an angular upper turn, a short downward projection and a rightward foot; these strokes do not securely separate i, j, or a modified 2.

The first digit has a clear sloping head and vertical 1 stem. The following heavily retraced loops have a strong right descender that continues below the lower loop and sweeps left, supporting final 9; an older 8-like looped layer is plausible but not securely separable, and no second first-digit 1 is independently visible.
